text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore moves further into electronic age with smart and cash cards and 50,000 to take part in its ID trials.
- Finance Minister Richard Hu launches cash-in-a-card payment system nationwide.

- Developers of the Vietnam-Singapore Industrial Park enters second phase of the project a year ahead of schedule after more than U.S. $75 million in capital investment has been committed by 13 companies in the last six months.
- Singapore Telecom is cutting international direct dialling rates to about 100 destinations by up to 46 percent.

- Malaysian stockbroker Rashid Hussain Bhd will merge DCB Bank and Kwong Yik Bank under DCB Holdings after acquiring Malayan Banking's 75 percent stake in Kwong Yik for Malaysian $2.6 billion in cash.
- European leaders faces crucial decisions at December summit on European Monetary Union.
- Malayan Banking to use Malaysian $1.87 billion in extraordinary gains from sale of its 75 percent stake in Kwong Yik Bank to finance acquisitions in Malaysia and around the region.
- Van der Horst moves into space imaging business.
- Hock Hua Bank Bhd likely to be injected into UCM Industrial Corporation Bhd's stockbroking arm.
- Shenzhen company which is developing a Singapore $1 billion commercial estate, seeks Singapore listed firm to take part in a share swap or property-share swap.
